mode: Read-only design review. No implementation, configuration change, deployment, publisher request or browser execution.
recommendation: Do not transplant the legacy Pages shortcut or enable global cache interception merely to fit Free CPU. Establish plan/CPU needs first. A narrow build-verified company HTML shortcut is feasible but does not make dynamic routes, RSC, quota or memory limits disappear. Keep the current validated route semantics until a separate implementation and parity gate are approved.

alternatives.option: Existing OpenNext path, appropriate Workers plan
alternatives.benefit: Preserves adapter-owned middleware, Next routing, response semantics and RSC handling with the smallest release delta.
alternatives.cost: Every HTML request may still enter Worker/NextServer; actual CPU and request volume must be assessed. Paid does not increase 128MB memory.

alternatives.benefit: Installed adapter resolves route ownership and can serve cached HTML/RSC/route bodies after routing middleware, avoiding NextServer import.
alternatives.risk: Global rather than company-only; it parses full JSON cache entries and hashes response bodies. Current default merges next.config headers after middleware headers, and later applies those headers to cache results. /guides?q= private/no-store and English/general404 no-store require specific parity proof before any enablement. No CPU guarantee.

alternatives.benefit: Can stream the exact build-produced HTML from a private asset path without runtime Next page loading, JSON parsing or per-request HTML hashing.
alternatives.risk: Must duplicate a carefully pinned subset of policy before bypassing middleware, or integrate after adapter middleware through version-sensitive internals. Strict cookie/RSC exclusions reduce hit coverage; Samsung calculator/OG/share/API traffic remains unaffected. This is optimization, not evidence of Free-plan compatibility.

legacyNotReusableAsIs: static-company-entrypoint imports next-on-pages/fetch-handler and a .vercel contract, while Workers uses .open-next/worker.js and ASSETS.
The generator expects .vercel/output/config.json and public <path>.html/<path>.rsc. OpenNext stores serialized .cache entries under cdn-cgi/_next_cache/<buildId>.

Next15.5.28 uses scoped cache keys route-cache/APP_PAGE/<ownerSHA256>/$/<pathname>; constructing old <pathname>.cache paths is incorrect. Derive ownership from the exact emitted build manifest/cache meta and validate it.
Legacy expected asset headers and Vary omit current Next-Router-Segment-Prefetch and Next-Url. Build/runtime response header parity must be re-established, including CSP.
Existing reviewed-source hashes intentionally fail on the current changed middleware/config. Do not update the hashes merely to bypass review.

buildGate: Only prerender routes whose owner is exactly /salary-db/[id]/page, initialRevalidateSeconds false, status200, complete HTML+RSC, and no PPR/fallback/redirect/custom response variation. Exclude every ambiguous entry.

Emit exact HTML bytes from the matching final build into a reserved /cdn-cgi/msy-static-company/<buildId>/<opaque-id>.html asset. Do not put app HTML at its public route path because assets-first routing would bypass middleware for all requests, including RSC.

Generate an allowlist mapping pathname to private asset, build-ID, HTML hash/size and approved response headers. Validate source/lock/config/middleware hashes and build identity together; no hand-written list of known company slugs.
Keep the ordinary OpenNext incremental cache and main handler for every noneligible request. Populate and release both private fast assets and adapter cache atomically with the same version.
Build-time QA/production markers must match their artifact; exact HTML byte reuse preserves normal visitor client ad guards and does not execute/load ads during inspection.
requestGate: Exact canonical https origin and host; GET or HEAD only; exact allowlisted pathname without encoded/slash-normalized aliases; initially no query or only a reviewed set of tracking parameters.

Fail to normal handler for cookie, authorization, range, conditionals, request cache bypass directives, RSC, next-action, prefetch/purpose, all Next/middleware/prerender transport headers, content-type or unknown variant headers.
Preserve allowlist-before-denylist UA policy, canonical redirect and bot403 semantics through shared/pinned code. Unknown or changed policy must disable the optimization.
Use env.ASSETS only for the fixed build-owned path; never fetch a user URL or construct a live same-zone request. No POST/read-body behavior belongs in the HTML shortcut.

Accept only expected200 HTML asset response without set-cookie; stream unchanged bytes; HEAD has null body. Strip internal transport headers and attach validated Next/security/cache/Vary headers. Unexpected asset response/error falls back after cancellation.
parityGate: Offline mocked ASSETS tests for every gate, cold/invalid cache, byte-exact HTML, HEAD semantics, immutable version mapping and fallback behavior.
Ad-free isolated Worker baseline/candidate HTTP comparisons for all allowlisted company routes: status, meaningful headers, bytes, embedded build/chunk references; no JavaScript execution.

Negative matrix: RSC1, segment prefetch, next-action, POST/OPTIONS, cookies/auth, each conditional/range, encoded paths, unknown queries, non-www, allowed/denied/missing UA, redirects, nonexistent company, query-private guides, English404, widgets and both private APIs.
Measure isolated code CPU as engineering evidence and actual authorized Worker CPU separately; wall time does not equal CPU. Test dynamic routes as well before claiming Free compatibility.

newAdapterBodyBoundary.distinction: Historical artifact mtime is2026-09-26. It is concrete former generated-code evidence, not a checksum assertion about the 2026-10-15 live Pages deployment. Imported helper arrayBuffer occurrences inspected were outgoing fetch/cache or test-proxy paths, not an unconditional inbound request buffer.
newAdapterBodyBoundary.impact: App storage and JSON validation remain bounded, but large/chunked bodies can allocate memory before those guards. 128MB Worker memory is unchanged by upgrading the plan.
newAdapterBodyBoundary.proposedMitigation: Before activation, bound both private POST bodies before the OpenNext converter, with exact route policy and bounded byte reading even when Content-Length is missing or false. On overflow cancel and return existing private/no-store error contract. If implemented in a custom entry, preserve request metadata/Cloudflare context for accepted requests; verify null body, UTF8 byte count, malformed length, encodings, slow/error streams and proxy-normalized aliases. Do not assume a header-only limit is sufficient.
newAdapterBodyBoundary.implementationStatus: Subsequently implemented by explicit parent request; see worker-body-boundary.json. Company HTML fastpath remains unimplemented.
